scenario.summary: An attacker used autonomous AI agents to compress weeks of intrusion tradecraft into a 10-hour campaign, breaching a web service to map the internal network and harvest secrets. The agents then escalated privileges through a secrets manager to hijack CI/CD pipelines and repurpose enterprise AI infrastructure for post-compromise operations.

meta.rationale: Focus on infrastructure hosting containerized web services and identities with administrative access to cloud control planes and CI/CD systems.
meta.hypothesis: An automated AI agent loop is conducting high-speed privilege escalation via secrets managers, tampering with CI/CD configurations, and hijacking cloud AI endpoints for external orchestration.

hunt.name: AI-Agentic Escalation and Infrastructure Hijacking
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the high-speed execution characteristic of agentic AI attacks, which compress weeks of manual red-teaming into hours. It targets the transition from failed to successful access (401 to 200 state shifts) against sensitive endpoints, followed by unauthorized modifications to Terraform configurations and bursty usage of enterprise AI services. By correlating these behaviors across authentication and file surfaces, we detect the methodical orchestration of an autonomous intruder.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '{{docker_package_pattern}}'
config.description: Find hosts running Docker, as the initial breach targeted containerized web services used to tunnel into the network.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames providing the attack surface. Silence indicates no Docker software was found in inventory.

primitive_config.label: Identify Docker-enabled infrastructure
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '{{docker_package_pattern}}'
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames providing the attack surface. Silence indicates no Docker software was found in inventory.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, actor_user_name, url_hostname, COUNT(CASE WHEN status_code = 401 THEN 1 END) AS unauthorized_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN status_code = 200 THEN 1 END) AS authorized_count, MIN(time) AS first_event, MAX(time) AS last_event FROM hb_http_activity WHERE status_code IN (200, 401) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, actor_user_name, url_hostname HAVING unauthorized_count > 0 AND authorized_count > 0 AND (julianday(MAX(time)) - julianday(MIN(time))) * 1440 <= 15
config.description: Detect automated agents successfully brute-forcing or harvesting secrets by looking for a transition from 401 to 200 within a tight 15-minute window.
config.expected_signal: A source IP or user showing multiple failures followed by success on a sensitive API. This is the primary indicator of an automated loop.
